messages.content: 如果一個球以5米/秒的速度直接向上投擲，它將達到什麼加速度？

function.name: calculate_maximum_height
function.description: Calculate the maximum height an object will reach if it's thrown straight upwards with an initial velocity, ignoring air resistance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity in meters per second. This is a float type value.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity in meters per second squared, default value is 9.8. This is a float type value.

message.content:
在地球表面，忽略空气阻力时，物体受到的重力加速度是一个常数，约为 \(g \approx 9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\)。  
当你把球以 5 m/s 的初速度垂直向上抛掷时，球在运动过程中会持续受到这个恒定的向下（负方向）的加速度。也就是说，球的加速度始终是 \(-9.8\ \text{m/s}^2\)，与其初速度大小无关。
message.reasoning: The user asks: "If a ball is thrown upward at 5 m/s, what acceleration will it reach?" Actually they ask: "它將達到什麼加速度" which means "what acceleration will it reach?" That seems odd: acceleration is constant -9.8 m/s^2 downward. They might want maximum height? But question says "accelerations". Maybe they mis-asked. We can interpret as "maximum height"? But we have tool to calculate maximum height. The user asked about acceleration. We could respond explaining that acceleration due to gravity is constant ~9.8 m/s^2 downward. So answer: -9.8 m/s^2. No need to call function.
